stories.title: Canada plans retaliatory tariffs after U.S. trade talks collapse
stories.summary: Canada says it will answer new 50% U.S. tariffs with dollar-for-dollar measures beginning September 8. The dispute covers goods including steel, dairy, appliances, farm equipment, paper and electronics, making the breakdown especially consequential for Michigan's cross-border manufacturing and agricultural economy.

stories.title: Judge dismisses federal challenge to Washtenaw County immigration policies
stories.summary: A federal judge ruled that Washtenaw County's sheriff, prosecutor and commissioners did not violate federal law by declining to assist with federal immigration enforcement. The ruling says the federal government cannot compel the county to use local jail space and resources for federal priorities.

stories.title: Michigan Republicans finalize 2026 statewide ticket
stories.summary: Republican delegates formally nominated state Rep. Jay DeBoyer as John James' running mate at the party convention in Mount Pleasant. The gathering emphasized state issues and party unity while rarely mentioning President Trump, whose approval ratings have weakened ahead of the general election.

stories.title: Michigan revenue runs modestly ahead of forecasts
stories.summary: Michigan collected about $3.1 billion in July, nearly 7% more than a year earlier. The general fund is roughly $455 million to $459 million above year-to-date projections, while the School Aid Fund is about $195 million to $220 million ahead, offering limited breathing room before expected difficult budget years.

stories.title: Detroit property-tax relief program returns
stories.summary: Wayne County's Pay as You Stay program is again available to qualifying Detroit homeowners, removing penalties, interest and fees from delinquent property taxes. Residents must first qualify for the income-based HOPE exemption; the 2026 enrollment deadline is November 6.

stories.title: Lathrup Village begins building its first city arboretum
stories.summary: Lathrup Village is turning public green space into an educational tree garden centered on Michigan-native species. The project is part of the city's broader green-infrastructure work to manage stormwater, reduce erosion and strengthen the community's mature tree canopy.

stories.title: Michigan-led effort revives an endangered butterfly population
stories.summary: Researchers and conservation partners have expanded the known U.S. population of the Poweshiek skipperling from nine wild butterflies in 2022 to roughly 1,300 in captive and restored populations. The effort combines breeding at John Ball Zoo with releases into restored habitat, including sites in Southeast Michigan.

stories.title: Plymouth Township board to consider its first master-plan update in 11 years
stories.summary: Plymouth Township trustees are scheduled to vote Aug. 25 on a master plan update that would replace the 2015 plan and guide future land-use and zoning decisions. The agenda also includes filling Trustee Mark Clinton’s vacant seat, a deputy police chief employment agreement, utility-budget items and public comment.

stories.title: Canton’s free household hazardous-waste round-up returns September 12
stories.summary: Canton residents can bring paint, motor oil, batteries, electronics, antifreeze and other accepted household hazardous waste to the township’s free Sept. 12 round-up. The event runs 9 a.m.–2 p.m. at the Division of Public Works building, 4847 Sheldon Road; a valid ID is required and the township warns of high volume.

stories.title: Arbor Hills landfill expansion heads to September public meeting
stories.summary: GFL Environmental plans to present a proposed 90-acre expansion of the Arbor Hills Landfill at the Washtenaw County Materials Management Planning Committee’s Sept. 9 meeting. The committee is expected to vote in December on consistency with the county’s materials-management plan, a step before county, municipal and state reviews; residents from nearby Plymouth and Northville townships have raised environmental and traffic concerns.

stories.title: McGregor Road lane restrictions expected during Ypsilanti Township chip-seal work
stories.summary: The Washtenaw County Road Commission began chip-seal work on McGregor Road between William Avenue and Tyler Road on Aug. 24. The road remains open, but intermittent lane restrictions and delays are expected for roughly two days, subject to weather.

stories.title: Ann Arbor student move-in brings weeklong traffic and parking changes
stories.summary: Ann Arbor’s city-approved University of Michigan move-in plan is in effect Aug. 24–30, with temporary one-way traffic, street closures and bagged parking meters near residence halls. The city lists changes including Division Street, Greene Street, Thompson Street and Madison Street; drivers should expect congestion and follow staffed barricades.

stories.title: Michigan voter-ID ballot proposal misses certification by a narrow margin
stories.summary: Michigan’s Board of State Canvassers declined to certify a proposed constitutional amendment tightening voter-ID and registration rules for the November ballot after disputed petition signatures left the campaign short. The campaign says it will go to court; any challenge faces a Sept. 4 deadline for final ballot wording.

stories.title: Plymouth-Canton board to vote on tentative teacher contract
stories.summary: The Plymouth-Canton school board is scheduled to vote Aug. 25 on ratifying a tentative agreement with the teachers union covering the 2026–27 and 2027–28 school years. The proposed agreement includes a new wage scale, planning-time and staffing provisions, and changes to class-size overage pay, leave and benefits as the district plans about $10 million in current-year cuts.

stories.title: Busch’s Canton remodel adds more than 1,600 products
stories.summary: Busch’s Fresh Food Market has completed a center-store remodel at 225 Canton Center Road, adding more than 1,600 products and reworking aisles, shelving, flooring and frozen-bakery placement. The grocer plans a public ribbon cutting at 10 a.m. Sept. 4, followed by a 10-day promotion and events through October.

stories.title: Canton’s free ARToberfest returns to Cherry Hill Village September 26
stories.summary: Canton Township and the Arts Warehouse at Cherry Hill will hold the fourth annual ARToberfest Family Fall Festival on Sept. 26, noon–4 p.m. The free event includes an artisan marketplace, live music, food trucks, the Cherry Hill Potters Guild’s fall sale, a youth art fair and family activities; the Canton Fine Arts Exhibition will also be on view through October.

stories.title: Plymouth Fall Festival returns to Kellogg Park September 11–13
stories.summary: Downtown Plymouth’s Fall Festival returns Sept. 11–13 with free admission, carnival rides, a craft show, live entertainment and nonprofit-run food fundraisers. Organizers list street closures near Kellogg Park and recommend checking the festival parking map; activities begin Friday afternoon and run through Sunday evening.

stories.title: Plymouth District Library seeks seniors’ input on technology classes
stories.summary: Plymouth District Library has opened a Tech Survey for Seniors to shape future programming on communication tools, online security, web services and artificial intelligence. The library also has free fall classes from September through November, including computer basics, Canva and job-search sessions; registration is required.

stories.title: Ann Arbor Camera Club exhibition opens at Canton’s Gallery at Cherry Hill
stories.summary: The Ann Arbor Camera Club’s “Collective Expressions in Photography” opens with a free reception Aug. 27, 6–8 p.m., at the Village Theater at Cherry Hill. The exhibit features work by 18 photographers across film and digital formats and remains on display through Sept. 20; regular gallery hours and appointment access are available.

stories.title: Wayne County reopens reduced-interest tax payment plan for Plymouth and Canton homeowners
stories.summary: Wayne County has reopened enrollment in its Interest Reduction Stipulated Payment Agreement program, which combines past-due property-tax years into one payment plan at 6% interest rather than 18%. Owner-occupants with a Principal Residence Exemption can enroll online or through the Treasurer’s Office; the program is intended to help prevent foreclosure.

stories.title: Plymouth Township’s July report shows permit growth and fire-station staffing strain
stories.summary: Plymouth Township issued 173 building permits in July, its highest monthly total of 2026, including permits for a Penske truck-service facility and Plymouth Exchange pump station. The same report says the Fire Department handled 409 calls, up 19% from a year earlier, and temporarily closed Station 2 for 81 hours because injuries reduced available staffing.

stories.title: Plymouth Township voters will decide parks-millage renewal in November
stories.summary: Plymouth Township voters will decide Nov. 3 whether to renew the existing 0.5-mill parks and recreation levy for four years, from 2027 through 2030. The levy funds maintenance and improvements at the township’s 14 parks; township officials identified playground replacements, trail work and pavilion repairs as potential priorities if it passes.

stories.title: Ann Arbor North University–Thayer project continues storm-sewer and streetscape work
stories.summary: Ann Arbor crews will continue storm-sewer, streetlight, planter-box, sidewalk and curb work on North University Avenue and Thayer Street during the week of Aug. 31. North University remains closed to through traffic between State and Fletcher through the project, while pedestrian access is maintained and cyclists must follow posted detours.
